pages.scope: For the reader with itchy bites who has looked and found no bed bugs. The build script rejects any slug that exists, is planned or scheduled, is a redirect source, carries a geo token, or whose meta title is over 48 characters; every collision path must exist.

Collisions were judged by meaning, not slug: each page lists the existing pages that answer the same or an overlapping question, what they rank for (Search Console), and how the two are kept apart (a regional pair with hreflang, a section trimmed to a summary plus a link, or a head term left with the existing page).

implementation: GuideCluster in lib/guides.ts allows only bed-bugs, ants, mice, cockroaches, mosquitoes, ticks, pest-control and garden. Pages in the new clusters (spiders, stinging-insects, flies, mites, fleas, household, kissing-bugs, scorpions, bites) are given guideCluster "pest-control" so they render today, but "Keep reading" cards and recirculation would then mix them with pest-control articles. Extending GuideCluster (plus CLUSTER_LABEL, CLUSTER_PILLAR and the FALLBACK map in scripts/build-article-index.mjs) before the first of these releases is the cleaner route.

Audience maps to the validator: "us" = no audience field (US English, Fahrenheit, inches); "ca" = audience "ca" with locale en-CA; "na" = audience "na" (US English with both units and both countries' regulators allowed).

Photos: photos.json covers ticks and mosquitoes only, so tick and mosquito pages are first in the release order. The validator refuses any figure not recorded there. Spiders, mites, fleas, bed bugs, midges and bites are being sourced; stinging insects, flies, kissing bugs, scorpions, household and garden pests still need sourcing (CDC PHIL and USDA/USGS images are public domain, the USGS Bee Inventory and Monitoring Lab covers bees and wasps; Bugwood images are mostly CC BY-NC and are not allowed). A page whose photos are not in hand cannot pass validation; its week moves.
parent null (natural-mosquito-repellent, permethrin-for-clothing) means the guide falls back to its cluster pillar (CLUSTER_PILLAR in lib/guides.ts).

Release order puts every new hub in the same or an earlier wave than its spokes; the release script needs a live hub before a spoke goes out, so if both fall on one Monday release the hub first or move it a week earlier.

Tools (/tools/what-bit-me, /tools/tick-identifier) are not on the Mediavine allow-list; adding them is the owner's call. They follow the /tools/what-bug-is-this pattern (real photos only, GA4 quiz events).

To schedule a page: copy its fields into data/god-build/extra-pages.json (slug, section, cluster -> use guideCluster until the type is extended, keyword, alsoTargets, h1Hint = title, scope, flags, minWords, parent, mustLink, audience when not "us"), then run node scripts/god-build-plan.mjs and node scripts/us-pages-plan.mjs. Check the head term against Search Console again on the day it is scheduled.
